title: POFM, valbonne-2023 Groupe B
scope: every exercise whose statement starts on the pages listed in documents; its solution may lie beyond them

grade_reasons.22001: 4e: tangent perpendicular to radius and perpendicular bisector, both in the 4e/5e course
grade_reasons.22002: 4e: equal tangent lengths proved inline with Pythagoras, then isosceles triangles and angle sum
grade_reasons.22003: 4e: isosceles triangles and angle sum; inscribed angle converse explained inline as a short lemma (convexity hypothesis added)
grade_reasons.22004: 4e: angle chasing with inscribed angles and the tangent-chord angle, both explained inline from the central angle
grade_reasons.22005: 4e: only the midpoint theorem and the circle with a given diameter; the uniqueness of the circle through three points
grade_reasons.22006: 2de: AM-GM for three numbers, proved inline from the factorisation of u^3+v^3+w^3-3uvw and squares, needs the cube root and the increasing cube function, known in 2de; not 3e because cube roots are not met at collège
grade_reasons.22007: Terminale: AM-GM for n numbers proved inline from ln t <= t-1 (study of a function with ln and derivative); n-th roots and ln need Terminale
grade_reasons.22008: 2de: AM-GM for three numbers proved inline (same lemma as 22006), cube roots and the cube function known in 2de
grade_reasons.22009: 3e: (t-1)^2 >= 0, (X+Y)^2 = (X-Y)^2 + 4XY and powers of positive numbers; the solution avoids square roots, so the identities of 3e are enough
grade_reasons.22010: 3e: expand (a_i - m)^2 and add, then a square root of positive numbers; identities are 3e
grade_reasons.22011: 2de: function Q to Q, substitutions, injectivity defined inline; the Cauchy equation on Q is solved inline by repeated addition (f(nx) = n f(x)), no induction needed
grade_reasons.22012: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence; here a single substitution suffices
grade_reasons.22013: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence; the contradiction uses only x and -x having the same square
grade_reasons.22014: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence
grade_reasons.22015: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence
grade_reasons.22016: 2de: functions N to N; a smallest-counterexample argument replaces the printed strong induction (Terminale), so no induction is needed
grade_reasons.22017: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence; the sign case split uses only x = 1
grade_reasons.22018: 2de: a function from R (or Q, N) to itself and substitutions are 2de vocabulary; injectivity and surjectivity are defined inline in one sentence; odd function and expanding products are 2de/3e
grade_reasons.22019: 3e: needs similar triangles; inscribed angle lemma and the perpendicular bisector of the common chord are explained inline
grade_reasons.22020: 3e: needs similar triangles (DBA ~ DAC, DBE ~ ABC); the tangent-chord angle is proved inline
grade_reasons.22021: 4e: angle chasing only; inscribed angle and the south pole lemma are proved inline, then an isosceles triangle
grade_reasons.22022: 4e: isosceles triangles, angle sums and congruent triangles; no tool beyond 4e
grade_reasons.22023: 4e: angle chasing, Thales in nested triangles and the south pole lemma proved inline; competition level, so 5 stars
grade_reasons.22024: 4e: circle of a diameter, inscribed angle, converse for a convex quadrilateral (proved inline), south pole lemma, cosine in a right triangle; IMO P1, so 5 stars
grade_reasons.22025: 2de: functional equation solved by one substitution and a check; functions are a 2de topic
grade_reasons.22026: 3e: the question asks for similar triangles; the central angle lemma is proved inline with isosceles triangles
grade_reasons.22027: 2de: inequality with squares; the fraction-grouping lemma is proved inline from (x - tp)^2 >= 0
grade_reasons.22028: 4e: congruent triangles (SAS) plus the inscribed angle lemma explained inline
grade_reasons.22029: 4e: one step from the definition of divisibility, literal calculation
grade_reasons.22030: 4e: parity of consecutive integers and a split by the remainder mod 3, written with 3k + 1 and 3k + 2
grade_reasons.22031: 4e: a divisor of a positive integer is not larger than it; one comparison
grade_reasons.22032: grade 8: pigeonhole on the 78 possible sums plus the removal of a common element, both tools from 4e; difficulty 3 because the student must see to compare sums of pairs, and to handle a shared element
grade_reasons.22033: grade 8: pigeonhole on the 16 blocks of 2 by 2 squares of the board; difficulty 2, a direct application once the board is cut
grade_reasons.22034: grade 8: only divisibility, the PPCM and pigeonhole on odd parts, all known in 4e; difficulty 5 because it combines the odd-part pigeonhole with a careful bound, competition level for 4e
grade_reasons.22035: grade 8: Erdos-Szekeres is proved inline with pigeonhole on pairs (c_i, d_i), and the triangle argument is Pythagoras in a coordinate grid, both 4e tools; difficulty 5 because it chains two non-obvious ideas
grade_reasons.22036: grade 10: needs the integer part and the fractional part of a real number, absolute values and irrational numbers, all 2de; difficulty 4 for the pigeonhole on fractional parts plus the argument for infinitely many
grade_reasons.22037: grade 8: only divisibility and the difference of two multiples, both 4e; difficulty 2, two steps once (n + 1)(n - 1) is spotted
grade_reasons.22038: grade 8: counting the sums and pigeonhole on their 2n + 1 possible values, all 4e; difficulty 3 like 7251, the student must think of counting the possible values
grade_reasons.22039: grade 9: needs prime factorisation and its uniqueness, which is 3e; difficulty 2, the counting is the product rule explained in the solution
grade_reasons.22040: grade 9: the factorisation (p - x)(p + y) = p^2 is 4e, but listing the divisors of p^2 uses prime factorisation, 3e; difficulty 3 for spotting the factorisation
grade_reasons.22041: 4e: only remainders in the division by 3 and the fact that adding a multiple of 3 keeps the remainder; difficulty 3 because the student must see the mod 3 invariant and also check the killing blow
grade_reasons.22042: 4e: chessboard and stripe colourings with counting, a case check at the corner, and a 2x2 block colouring; nothing beyond counting and parity; difficulty 4 because four parts each need their own idea
grade_reasons.22043: 4e: parity of the number of 1s, checked in three cases; difficulty 2, a direct use of a parity invariant
grade_reasons.22044: 4e: only the Euclidean division n = 10q + r and the fact that a sum or difference of multiples of 7 (or 13) is a multiple; no congruences needed; difficulty 2, two short computations per direction
grade_reasons.22045: 4e: remainders of a product shown by expanding (19k + r)(19l + s), a table of powers of 8, and the remainder of the exponent by 6; all remainder arithmetic, case 1 of the brief; difficulty 4 for the two-level tower
grade_reasons.22046: 3e: needs that every integer >= 2 is a product of primes (prime factorisation, 3e), plus remainders of products checked by expanding (4e); difficulty 4, an Euclid-style construction to adapt twice
grade_reasons.22047: 4e: squares of even and odd numbers in the division by 4 and by 8, found by expanding (2m + 1)^2, and parity; difficulty 3, the second equation needs the idea of halving and then looking at remainders by 8
grade_reasons.22048: Terminale, maths expertes (checked, kept): the proof rests on inverses modulo p, built from Euclid's lemma (a prime dividing a product divides a factor), i.e. congruences used as a theory, case 2 of the brief, the same family as Fermat's little theorem which the collection keeps at grade 12; a remainder-only version for 3e would have to teach the inverse theory inside the exercise; difficulty 3, guided in four questions, the pairing is the idea
grade_reasons.22049: Terminale, maths expertes (checked, kept): Euler's criterion, proved by pairing each x with the y such that xy ≡ n mod p; needs inverses modulo p and Euclid's lemma as in 22048 (case 2); no polynomial theory, unlike the printed solution; difficulty 4, one statement to prove with no guidance
grade_reasons.22050: 4e: congruences explained in a few lines as equal remainders (case 1), expanding (x + 3b)^2 by distributivity, and a table of squares modulo 5; difficulty 4 because the student must find the shift by 3b and then separate five cases
grade_reasons.22051: Terminale, maths expertes (checked, kept): uses Fermat's little theorem and Euclid's lemma (Gauss) as known results, both named in case 2 of the brief; difficulty 3, apply Fermat twice, handle p | M, then combine
grade_reasons.22052: Terminale, maths expertes: needs Fermat little theorem for one direction and Wilson theorem (proved inline from inverses modulo p) for the other, case 2 of the brief, same family as 22048 and 22049; difficulty 4, two directions plus an Euclid-type infinity proof
grade_reasons.22053: Terminale, maths expertes: Fermat little theorem plus a Bezout relation between the exponents q and p-1, case 2 of the brief; no lower-grade route since q | p-1 is an order statement; difficulty 4, the Bezout-on-exponents idea plus a symmetric contradiction
grade_reasons.22054: 4e: only the multiplication principle, used step by step (fix the first player, then repeat), no factorials needed for the answer 1 x 3 x ... x (2n-1); not lower since the database starts at 4e; difficulty 3, the idea is to always pair the first unpaired player so nothing is counted twice
grade_reasons.22055: 3e: the only tool beyond counting by hand is the number of ways to choose k objects among N, explained inline (ordered choices divided by the number of orders, case 1); the rest is a bijection between 0/1 words and sets of change positions; 3e rather than 4e because the inline binomial count and a general-n answer are heavy for a 4e club; difficulty 4, the padding trick (add 1 in front and 0 at the end) is a real idea and both directions of the bijection must be checked
grade_reasons.22056: 4e: parity and the square of an odd number 4k(k+1)+1 (4e expanding), remainders by 8; not lower, the database starts at 4e; difficulty 2, two short steps
grade_reasons.22057: 4e: congruences as remainders explained inline (case 1) and a table of remainders of r^2 and r^4 mod 13 replaces Fermat; difficulty 3, the idea is to look mod 13 (26 = 2 x 13 and 12 = 13 - 1)
grade_reasons.22058: 4e: last digit of a product depends only on last digits, cycle 3, 9, 7, 1, and 2024 = 4 x 506; difficulty 2, two steps
grade_reasons.22059: 4e: cubes mod 9 from expanding (3k +- 1)^3, congruences as remainders (case 1); difficulty 3, the idea is to choose 9
grade_reasons.22060: 3e: a^2 - 4 = (a - 2)(a + 2) and unique prime factorisation, both 3e; not 4e because of the identity; difficulty 3, seeing the difference of squares is the idea
grade_reasons.22061: 3e: factorisation of 2^p + 3^p for odd p checked by expanding (telescoping, case 1), remainders mod 5 (case 1) and prime factorisation (3e); the source uses the binomial formula (Terminale), avoided here; difficulty 4, several ideas and cases p = 2, p = 5
grade_reasons.22062: 4e: square roots, irreducible fractions and parity are all 4e tools; the brief lists sqrt(2) irrational as a 2de course result, but the proof itself uses nothing beyond 4e, so the lowest-grade rule puts it here; difficulty 3, the absurd hypothesis and the parity chain are the idea
grade_reasons.22063: 4e: fractions and ordering a <= b <= c to bound a, then two small cases; difficulty 3, the symmetry plus bounding idea
grade_reasons.22064: 3e: a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b) (3e) and divisibility with inequalities; difficulty 4, bounding a - b <= 1 then two cases, one with a size argument (APMO 2002)
grade_reasons.22065: 4e: only logic about who shares a vote with whom, then the pigeonhole count 3 x 13 < 40 and a three-row example; not lower since the database starts at 4e; difficulty 4, a proof (all votes go to three animators) plus a separate construction
grade_reasons.22066: 4e: coordinates in a repere (cycle 4) and the midpoint abscissa as an average, justified inline with a translation; not lower since the database starts at 4e; difficulty 4, needs a construction, a good choice of axes, and the extremal-point count

similar triangles plus the tangent-chord lemma; nothing from 1re is needed

south pole lemma via inscribed angles, pure angle chasing

only the product rule for counting subsets and pigeonhole on their sums; nothing beyond 3e
pigeonhole on small squares and the area of a triangle inside a square, all 4e
Erdos-Szekeres by pigeonhole on pairs of lengths, pure 4e tools; keep difficulty 5
prime factorisation and pigeonhole on remainders, all 3e
pigeonhole on fractional parts, needs only integer part and irrationals from 2de
Euclidean division by 4, the product of numbers 4k + 1, and a prime factor of N; prime factorisation is 3e. Difficulty 5 also looks high for 3e, 4 seems right
the factorisation of x^b - 1 is checked by expanding, primes are 4e; nothing beyond 3e
the factorisation of a^p + b^p for odd p is checked by expanding, and the odd part of n replaces the prime factorisation; nothing beyond 3e
the sweep argument, or the shortest total length with the triangle inequality, is 4e
same problem as 8840, same 4e argument; the two are already linked same_as, so 8341 would then become a same-grade copy and one of them should be retired
parity of a sum, and |a-b| has the parity of a+b; pure 4e
parity of the sum of the numbers on the board, pure 4e

the discriminant b^2-4ac is used only as an expression that does not change; checking it needs only expanding, which is 3e (no second degree theory needed)
colouring the 2x2 blocks in a chessboard pattern and counting cells is 4e
same problem as 0508, same 4e block colouring
y^k - 1 is a multiple of y - 1, by expanding (y - 1)(y^(k-1) + ... + 1) or by remainders explained in a few lines; nothing from 1re

expanding (n - 1)^3 and (n + 1)^3, and one of three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3: all 4e; 4803 (grade 12) is its same_as copy and would then be redundant
p^2 - 1 = (p - 1)(p + 1), a product of two consecutive even numbers, and one of p - 1, p, p + 1 is a multiple of 3: 3e at most
squares in the division by 8 come from (2m + 1)^2 = 4m(m + 1) + 1 and parity: 4e
